findings.evidence: 6 respondents affected (e.g., R0028, R0122, R0243, R0259, R0425, R0502), where sum is 4 (prorated raw 4.5), scored as 4 and 'none-minimal' instead of 5 and 'mild'.
findings.description: When prorating a PHQ-9 score with 1 missing item resulting in a half-integer (e.g. sum of 4 giving 4.5), the scoring pipeline rounds half-to-even (standard Python round()) instead of following the study convention of rounding halves up (4.5 to 5). This affects the total and consequently the severity band.

findings.evidence: 2 respondents affected (R0328, R0502), where sum is 9 (prorated raw 10.5), scored as 10 instead of 11.
findings.description: When prorating a GAD-7 score with 1 missing item resulting in a half-integer (e.g. sum of 9 giving 10.5), the scoring pipeline rounds half-to-even (standard Python round()) instead of following the study convention of rounding halves up (10.5 to 11).
